Philippians 1:1	Paul (humble) and Timothy (honoring God), servants {douloi} of Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves), To all the saints (holy ones) in Christ Jesus at Philippi, together with the overseers and deacons {diakonois}:
Philippians 1:2	Grace and peace to you⁺ from God {Theou} our Father and the Lord {Kyriou} Jesus (YHWH saves) Christ (the Anointed One).
Philippians 1:3	I thank my God {Theō} every time I remember you⁺.
Philippians 1:4	In every prayer for all of you⁺, I always pray with joy,
Philippians 1:5	because of your⁺ partnership {koinōnia} in the gospel (good news) from the first day until now,
Philippians 1:6	being confident of this, that He who began a good work in you⁺ will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves).
Philippians 1:7	It is right for me to feel this way about all of you⁺, since I have you⁺ in my heart. For in my chains and in my defense and confirmation of the gospel (good news), you⁺ are all partners in grace with me.
Philippians 1:8	God is my witness how I long for all of you⁺ with the affection of Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves).
Philippians 1:9	And this is my prayer: that your⁺ love {agapē} may abound more and more in knowledge (discernment) and depth of insight,
Philippians 1:10	so that you⁺ may be able to test and prove what is best and may be pure and blameless for the day of Christ (the Anointed One),
Philippians 1:11	filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus (YHWH saves) Christ (the Anointed One), to the glory {doxan} and praise (approval) of God {Theou}.
Philippians 1:12	Now I want you⁺ to know, brothers (and sisters), that my circumstances have actually served to advance the gospel (good news).
Philippians 1:13	As a result, it has become clear throughout the whole palace guard (all the Praetorium) and to everyone else that I am in chains for Christ (the Anointed One).
Philippians 1:14	And most of the brothers (and sisters), confident in the Lord {Kyriō} by my chains, now dare more greatly to speak the word [the word of God] without fear.
Philippians 1:15	It is true that some preach Christ (the Anointed One) out of envy and rivalry, but others out of goodwill.
Philippians 1:16	The latter do so in love {agapēs}, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the gospel (good news).
Philippians 1:17	The former, however, preach Christ (the Anointed One) out of selfish ambition, not sincerely, supposing that they can add to the distress of my chains.
Philippians 1:18	What then is the issue \What then?/? Just this: that in every way, whether by false motives or true, Christ (the Anointed One) is preached. And in this I rejoice. Yes, and I will continue to rejoice,
Philippians 1:19	because I know that through your⁺ prayers and the provision of the Spirit {Pneumatos} of Jesus (YHWH saves) Christ (the Anointed One), my distress will turn out for my deliverance.
Philippians 1:20	I eagerly expect and hope that I will in no way be ashamed, but will have complete boldness so that now as always Christ (the Anointed One) will be exalted in my body, whether by life or by death.
Philippians 1:21	For to me, to live is Christ (the Anointed One), and to die is gain.
Philippians 1:22	But if I go on living in the body (flesh), this will mean fruitful labor for me. So what shall I choose? I do not know.
Philippians 1:23	I am torn between the two. I desire to depart and be with Christ (the Anointed One), which is far better indeed.
Philippians 1:24	But it is more necessary for you⁺ that I remain in the body (flesh).
Philippians 1:25	Convinced of this, I know that I will remain and will continue with all of you⁺ for your⁺ progress and joy in the faith,
Philippians 1:26	so that through my coming to you⁺ again your⁺ exultation in Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves) will resound on account of me.
Philippians 1:27	Nevertheless, conduct yourselves in a manner worthy of the gospel (good news) of Christ (the Anointed One). Then, whether I come and see you⁺ or only hear about you⁺ in my absence, I will know that you⁺ stand firm in one spirit {pneumati}, contending together as one (striving together with one mind) for the faith of the gospel,
Philippians 1:28	without being frightened in any way by those who oppose you. This is a clear sign of their destruction (ruin) but of your⁺ salvation, and it is from God {Theou}.
Philippians 1:29	For it has been granted to you⁺ on behalf of Christ (the Anointed One) not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer for Him,
Philippians 1:30	since you are encountering the same struggle you⁺ saw I had, and now hear that I still have.
Philippians 2:1	Therefore if you have any encouragement in Christ (the Anointed One), if any comfort from His love {agapēs}, if any fellowship {koinōnia} with the Spirit {Pneumatos}, if any affection and compassion,
Philippians 2:2	then make my joy complete by being like-minded, having the same love {agapēn}, being united in spirit and purpose.
Philippians 2:3	Do nothing out of selfish ambition or empty pride, but in humility consider others more important than yourselves.
Philippians 2:4	Each of you should look not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others.
Philippians 2:5	Let this mind be in you⁺ which was also in Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves):
Philippians 2:6	Who, existing in the form of God {Theou}, did not consider equality with God {Theō} something to be grasped (something to be exploited),
Philippians 2:7	but emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant {doulou}, being made in human likeness.
Philippians 2:8	And being found in appearance as a man, He humbled Himself and became obedient to death—even death on a cross.
Philippians 2:9	Therefore God {Theos} exalted Him to the highest place and gave Him the name above all names,
Philippians 2:10	that at the name of Jesus (YHWH saves) every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth,
Philippians 2:11	and every tongue (language) confess that Jesus (YHWH saves) Christ (the Anointed One) is Lord {KYRIOS}, to the glory {doxan} of God {Theou} the Father.
Philippians 2:12	Therefore, my beloved {agapētoi}, just as you⁺ have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now even more in my absence, continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
Philippians 2:13	For it is God {Theos} who works in you⁺ to will and to act on behalf of His good purpose.
Philippians 2:14	Do everything without complaining or arguing,
Philippians 2:15	so that you⁺ may be blameless and pure, children of God {Theou} without fault in a crooked and perverse generation <Deu 32:5>, in which you⁺ shine as lights in the world
Philippians 2:16	as you hold forth the word of life, in order that I may boast on the day of Christ (the Anointed One) that I did not run or labor in vain.
Philippians 2:17	But even if I am being poured out like a drink offering on the sacrifice and service of your⁺ faith, I am glad and rejoice with all of you⁺.
Philippians 2:18	So you⁺ too should be glad and rejoice with me.
Philippians 2:19	Now I hope in the Lord {Kyriō} Jesus (YHWH saves) to send Timothy (honoring God) to you⁺ soon, that I also may be cheered when I learn how you⁺ are doing.
Philippians 2:20	I have nobody else like him who will genuinely care for your⁺ needs.
Philippians 2:21	For all the others look after their own interests, not those of Jesus (YHWH saves) Christ (the Anointed One).
Philippians 2:22	But you⁺ know Timothy’s proven worth, that as a child with his father he has served with me to advance the gospel (good news).
Philippians 2:23	So I hope to send him as soon as I see what happens with me.
Philippians 2:24	And I trust in the Lord {Kyriō} that I myself will come soon.
Philippians 2:25	But I thought it necessary to send back to you⁺ Epaphroditus, my brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier, who is also your⁺ messenger (apostle) and minister to my needs.
Philippians 2:26	For he has been longing for all of you⁺ and is distressed because you⁺ heard he was ill.
Philippians 2:27	He was sick indeed, nearly unto death. But God {Theos} had mercy on him, and not only on him but also on me, to spare me sorrow upon sorrow.
Philippians 2:28	Therefore I am all the more eager to send him, so that when you see him again you⁺ may rejoice, and I may be less anxious.
Philippians 2:29	Welcome him in the Lord {Kyriō} with great joy, and honor men like him,
Philippians 2:30	because he nearly died for the work of Christ (the Anointed One), risking his life {psychē} to make up for your⁺ deficit of service to me.
Philippians 3:1	Finally, my brothers (and sisters), rejoice in the Lord {Kyriō}. It is no trouble for me to write the same things to you⁺ again, and it is a safeguard for you⁺.
Philippians 3:2	Watch out for those dogs, those workers of evil, those mutilators of the flesh!
Philippians 3:3	For it is we who are the circumcision, we who worship by the Spirit {Pneumati} of God {Theou}, who glory in Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves), and who put no confidence in the flesh—
Philippians 3:4	though I myself could have such confidence. If anyone else thinks he has grounds for confidence in the flesh, I have more:
Philippians 3:5	circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel (He wrestles with God), of the tribe of Benjamin (son of the right hand); a Hebrew of Hebrews; as to the law, a Pharisee;
Philippians 3:6	as to zeal, persecuting the church {ekklēsian}; as to righteousness in the law, faultless.
Philippians 3:7	But whatever was gain to me I count as loss for the sake of Christ (the Anointed One).
Philippians 3:8	More than that, I count all things as loss compared to the surpassing excellence of knowing Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves) my Lord {Kyriou}, for whom I have lost all things. I consider them rubbish, that I may gain Christ
Philippians 3:9	and be found in Him, not having my own righteousness from the law, but that which is through faith in Christ (through the faithfulness of Christ), the righteousness from God {Theou} on the basis of faith.
Philippians 3:10	I want to know Christ and the power {dynamin} of His resurrection (rising again) and the fellowship {koinōnian} of His sufferings, being conformed to Him in His death,
Philippians 3:11	and so, somehow, to attain to the resurrection from the dead.
Philippians 3:12	Not that I have already obtained all this, or have already been made perfect, but I press on to take hold of that for which Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves) took hold of me.
Philippians 3:13	Brothers, I do not consider myself yet to have taken hold of it. But one thing I do: Forgetting what is behind and straining toward what is ahead,
Philippians 3:14	I press on toward the goal to win the prize of God’s {Theou} heavenly calling in Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves).
Philippians 3:15	All of us who are mature (complete) should embrace this point of view. And if you⁺ think differently about some issue, God {Theos} will reveal this to you⁺ as well.
Philippians 3:16	Nevertheless, we must live up to what we have already attained.
Philippians 3:17	Join one another in following my example, brothers (and sisters), and carefully observe those who walk according to the pattern we set for you⁺.
Philippians 3:18	For as I have often told you⁺ before, and now say again even with tears: Many live as enemies of the cross of Christ (the Anointed One).
Philippians 3:19	Their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and their glory {doxa} is in their shame. Their minds are set on earthly things.
Philippians 3:20	But our citizenship is in heaven, and we eagerly await a Savior {Sōtēra} from there, the Lord {Kyrion} Jesus (YHWH saves) Christ (the Anointed One),
Philippians 3:21	who, by the power that enables Him to subject all things to Himself, will transform our lowly bodies to be like His glorious body.

Colossians 1:1	Paul (humble), an apostle (sent one) of Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves) by the will of God {Theou}, and Timothy (honoring God) our brother,
Colossians 1:2	To the saints (holy ones) and faithful brothers (and sisters) in Christ (the Anointed One) at Colossae: Grace and peace to you⁺ from God {Theou} our Father [God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ].
Colossians 1:3	We always thank God {Theō}, the Father of our Lord {Kyriou} Jesus (YHWH saves) Christ (the Anointed One), when we pray for you⁺,
Colossians 1:4	because we have heard about your⁺ faith in Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves) and your⁺ love {agapēn} for all the saints (holy ones)—
Colossians 1:5	the faith and love proceeding from the hope stored up for you⁺ in heaven, of which you⁺ have already heard in the word of truth, the gospel (good news)
Colossians 1:6	that has come to you⁺. All over the world this gospel is bearing fruit and growing, just as it has been doing among you⁺ since the day you⁺ heard it and truly understood the grace of God {Theou}.
Colossians 1:7	You⁺ learned it from Epaphras, our beloved {agapētou} fellow servant {syndoulou}, who is a faithful minister {diakonos} of Christ (the Anointed One) on our [your] behalf,
Colossians 1:8	and who also informed us of your⁺ love {agapēn} in the Spirit {Pneumati}.
Colossians 1:9	For this reason, since the day we heard about you, we have not stopped praying for you⁺ and asking God to fill you⁺ with the knowledge (discernment) of His will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding,
Colossians 1:10	so that you may walk in a manner worthy of the Lord {Kyriou} and may please Him in every way: bearing fruit in every good work, growing in the knowledge (discernment) of God {Theou},
Colossians 1:11	being strengthened with all power {dynamei} according to His glorious might so that you may have full endurance (perseverance) and patience, and joyfully
Colossians 1:12	giving thanks to the Father, who has qualified you⁺ [us] to share in the inheritance of the saints (holy ones) in the light.
Colossians 1:13	He has rescued us from the dominion of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of His beloved Son,
Colossians 1:14	in whom we have redemption [redemption through His blood,], the forgiveness of sins.
Colossians 1:15	The Son is the image of the invisible God {Theou}, the firstborn over all creation.
Colossians 1:16	For in Him all things were created, things in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities. All things were created through Him and for Him.
Colossians 1:17	He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together.
Colossians 1:18	And He is the head of the body, the church {ekklēsias}; He is the beginning and firstborn from among the dead, so that in all things He may have preeminence.
Colossians 1:19	For God was pleased to have all His fullness dwell in Him,
Colossians 1:20	and through Him to reconcile to Himself all things, whether things on earth or things in heaven, by making peace through the blood of His cross.
Colossians 1:21	Once you⁺ were alienated from God and were hostile in your minds, engaging in evil deeds (acts).
Colossians 1:22	But now He has reconciled you by Christ’s physical body through death to present you⁺ holy, unblemished (blameless), and blameless in His presence—
Colossians 1:23	if indeed you⁺ continue in your faith, established and firm, not moved from the hope of the gospel (good news) you⁺ heard, which has been proclaimed to every creature (in all creation) under heaven, and of which I, Paul (humble), have become a servant {diakonos}.
Colossians 1:24	Now I rejoice in my sufferings for you⁺, and I fill up in my flesh what is lacking in regard to Christ’s afflictions for the sake of His body, which is the church {ekklēsia}.
Colossians 1:25	I became its servant {diakonos} by the commission God {Theou} gave me to fully proclaim to you⁺ the word of God,
Colossians 1:26	the mystery that was hidden for ages and generations but is now revealed (made clear) to His saints (holy ones).
Colossians 1:27	To them God {Theos} has chosen to make known among the Gentiles {ethnesin} the glorious riches of this mystery, which is Christ (the Anointed One) in you⁺, the hope of glory {doxēs}.
Colossians 1:28	We proclaim Him, admonishing and teaching {didaskontes} everyone with all wisdom, so that we may present everyone perfect (fully mature) in Christ (the Anointed One).
Colossians 1:29	To this end I also labor, striving with all His energy working powerfully within me.

Colossians 2:3	in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
Colossians 2:4	I say this so that no one will deceive you⁺ by smooth rhetoric.
Colossians 2:5	For although I am absent from you⁺ in body (flesh), I am present with you⁺ in spirit {pneumati}, and I delight to see your⁺ orderly condition and firm faith in Christ (the Anointed One).
Colossians 2:6	Therefore, just as you⁺ have received Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves) as Lord {Kyrion}, continue to walk in Him,
Colossians 2:7	rooted and built up in Him, established in the faith as you⁺ were taught, and overflowing with thankfulness.
Colossians 2:8	See to it that no one takes you⁺ captive through philosophy and empty deception, which are based on human tradition and the spiritual forces of the world rather than on Christ (the Anointed One).
Colossians 2:9	For in Christ all the fullness of the Deity {Theotētos} dwells in bodily form.
Colossians 2:10	And you⁺ have been made complete in Christ, who is the head over every ruler and authority.

Colossians 2:12	And having been buried with Him in baptism (submersion), you⁺ were raised with Him through your faith in the power of God {Theou}, who raised Him from the dead.
Colossians 2:13	When you⁺ were dead in your trespasses and in the uncircumcision of your⁺ sinful nature, God made you alive with Christ. He forgave us all our trespasses,
Colossians 2:14	having canceled the debt ascribed to us in the decrees that stood against us. He took it away, nailing it to the cross!
Colossians 2:15	And having disarmed the powers and authorities, He made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them by the cross.
Colossians 2:16	Therefore let no one judge you⁺ by what you eat or drink, or with regard to a feast, a New Moon, or a Sabbath.
Colossians 2:17	These are a shadow of the things to come, but the body that casts it belongs to Christ \but the body is of the Christ/.
Colossians 2:18	Do not let anyone who delights in false humility and the worship of angels (messengers) disqualify you⁺ with speculation about what he has seen. Such a person is puffed up without basis by his unspiritual mind.
Colossians 2:19	He has lost connection to the head, from whom the whole body, supported and knit together by its joints and ligaments, grows as God {Theou} causes it to grow.
Colossians 2:20	If you⁺ have died with Christ (the Anointed One) to the spiritual forces of the world, why, as though you still belonged to the world, do you⁺ submit to its regulations:
Colossians 2:21	“Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch!
Colossians 2:22	These will all perish with use, because they are based on human commands and teachings {didaskalias}.
Colossians 2:23	Such restrictions indeed have an appearance of wisdom, with their self-prescribed worship, their false humility, and their harsh treatment of the body; but they are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh.
Colossians 3:1	Therefore, since you⁺ have been raised with Christ (the Anointed One), strive for the things above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God {Theou}.
Colossians 3:2	Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.
Colossians 3:3	For you⁺ died, and your⁺ life is now hidden with Christ (the Anointed One) in God {Theō}.
Colossians 3:4	When Christ (the Anointed One), who is your⁺ [our] life, appears, then you⁺ also will appear with Him in glory {doxē}.
Colossians 3:5	Put to death, therefore, the components of your earthly nature: sexual immorality {porneian}, impurity (uncleanness), lust, evil desires, and greed, which is idolatry.
Colossians 3:6	Because of these, the wrath of God {Theou} is coming on the sons of disobedience.
Colossians 3:7	When you⁺ lived among them, you⁺ also used to walk in these ways.
Colossians 3:8	But now you⁺ must put aside all such things as these: anger, rage, malice, slander (blaspheme), and filthy language from your⁺ lips.
Colossians 3:9	Do not lie to one another, since you have taken off the old self with its practices,
Colossians 3:10	and have put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge (discernment) in the image of its Creator.
Colossians 3:11	Here there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian (foreigner), Scythian, slave {doulos}, or free, but Christ is all and is in all.
Colossians 3:12	Therefore, as the elect of God {Theou}, holy and beloved {ēgapēmenoi}, clothe yourselves with hearts of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.
Colossians 3:13	Bear with one another and forgive any complaint you⁺ may have against someone else. Forgive as the Lord {Kyrios} forgave you⁺.
Colossians 3:14	And over all these virtues put on love {agapēn}, which is the bond of perfect unity.
Colossians 3:15	Let the peace of Christ (the Anointed One) rule in your⁺ hearts, for to this you⁺ were called as members of one body. And be thankful.
Colossians 3:16	Let the word of Christ (the Anointed One) richly dwell within you⁺ as you teach {didaskontes} and admonish one another with all wisdom, and as you sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs with gratitude in your⁺ hearts to God {Theō}.
Colossians 3:17	And whatever you⁺ do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord {Kyriou} Jesus (YHWH saves), giving thanks to God {Theō} the Father through Him.
Colossians 3:18	Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord {Kyriō}.
Colossians 3:19	Husbands, love {agapate} your wives and do not be harsh with them.
Colossians 3:20	Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing to the Lord {Kyriō}.

1 Timothy 1:1	Paul (humble), an apostle (sent one) of Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves) by the command of God {Theou} our Savior and of Christ Jesus our hope,
1 Timothy 1:2	To Timothy (honoring God), my true child in the faith: Grace, mercy (compassion), and peace from God {Theou} the Father and Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves) our Lord {kyriou}.
1 Timothy 1:3	As I urged you on my departure to Macedonia, you should stay on at Ephesus (appealing) to instruct certain men not to teach false doctrines
1 Timothy 1:4	or devote themselves to myths and endless genealogies, which promote speculation rather than the stewardship of God’s work, which is by faith \rather than the stewardship of God in faith/.
1 Timothy 1:5	The goal of our instruction is the love {agapē} that comes from a pure heart, a clear conscience, and a sincere faith.
1 Timothy 1:6	Some have strayed from these ways and turned aside to empty talk.
1 Timothy 1:7	They want to be teachers of the law, but they do not understand what they are saying or that which they so confidently assert.
1 Timothy 1:8	Now we know that the law is good, if one uses it legitimately.
1 Timothy 1:9	We realize that law is not enacted for the righteous, but for the lawless and rebellious, for the ungodly and sinful, for the unholy and profane, for killers of father or mother, for murderers,
1 Timothy 1:10	for the sexually immoral, for homosexuals, for slave traders (for kidnappers) and liars and perjurers, and for anyone else who is averse to sound teaching {didaskalia}
1 Timothy 1:11	that agrees with the glorious gospel (good news) of the blessed God {Theou}, with which I have been entrusted.
1 Timothy 1:12	I thank Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves) our Lord {Kyriō}, who has strengthened me, that He considered me faithful and appointed me to service {diakonian}.
1 Timothy 1:13	I was formerly a blasphemer, a persecutor, and a violent man; yet because I had acted in ignorance and unbelief, I was shown mercy.
1 Timothy 1:14	And the grace of our Lord {Kyriou} overflowed to me, along with the faith and love {agapēs} that are in Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves).
1 Timothy 1:15	This is a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance: Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves) came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the worst.
1 Timothy 1:16	But for this very reason I was shown mercy, so that in me, the worst of sinners, Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves) might display His perfect patience as an example to those who would believe in Him for eternal life.
1 Timothy 1:17	Now to the King eternal, immortal, and invisible, the only God {Theō}, be honor and glory {doxa} forever \to the ages/ and ever. Amen.
1 Timothy 1:18	Timothy (honoring God), my child, I entrust you with this command in keeping with the previous prophecies about you, so that by them you may fight the good fight,
1 Timothy 1:19	holding on to faith and a good conscience, which some have rejected and thereby shipwrecked their faith.
1 Timothy 1:20	Among them are Hymenaeus and Alexander (defending men), whom I have handed over to Satan (the adversary) to be taught not to blaspheme.
1 Timothy 2:1	First of all, then, I urge that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgiving be offered for everyone—
1 Timothy 2:2	for kings and all those in authority—so that we may lead tranquil and quiet lives in all godliness and dignity.
1 Timothy 2:3	This is good and pleasing in the sight of God {Theou} our Savior,
1 Timothy 2:4	who wants everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge (discernment) of the truth.
1 Timothy 2:5	For there is one God {Theos}, and there is one mediator (reconciler) between God {Theou} and men, the man Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves),
1 Timothy 2:6	who gave Himself as a ransom for all—the testimony that was given at just the right time.
1 Timothy 2:7	For this reason I was appointed as a preacher, an apostle (sent one), and a faithful and true teacher {didaskalos} of the Gentiles {ethnōn}. I am telling the truth; I am not lying about anything.
1 Timothy 2:8	Therefore I want the men everywhere (in every place of worship) to pray, lifting up holy hands, without anger or dissension.
1 Timothy 2:9	Likewise, I want the women to adorn themselves with respectable apparel, with modesty, and with self-control, not with braided hair or gold or pearls or expensive clothes,
1 Timothy 2:10	but with good deeds (acts), as is proper for women who profess to worship God {theosebeian}.
1 Timothy 2:11	A woman (wife) must learn in quietness and full submissiveness.
1 Timothy 2:12	I do not permit a woman to teach {didaskein} or to exercise authority over a man (over her husband); she is to remain quiet.
1 Timothy 2:13	For Adam (man) was formed first, and then Eve (living).
1 Timothy 2:14	And it was not Adam (man) who was deceived, but the woman who was deceived and fell into transgression.
1 Timothy 2:15	Women, however, will be saved \She, however, will be saved/ through childbearing, if they continue in faith, love {agapē}, and holiness, with self-control.
1 Timothy 3:1	This is a trustworthy saying: If anyone aspires to be an overseer, he desires a noble task.
1 Timothy 3:2	An overseer, then, must be above reproach, the husband of but one wife (faithful to his wife), temperate, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, able to teach {didaktikon},
1 Timothy 3:3	not dependent on wine, not violent but gentle, peaceable, and free of the love of money.
1 Timothy 3:4	An overseer must manage his own household well and keep his children under control, with complete dignity.
1 Timothy 3:5	For if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how can he care for the church {ekklēsias} of God {Theou}?
1 Timothy 3:6	He must not be a recent convert, or he may become conceited and fall under the same condemnation as the devil {diabolou}.
1 Timothy 3:7	Furthermore, he must have a good reputation with outsiders, so that he will not fall into disgrace and into the snare of the devil {diabolou}.
1 Timothy 3:8	Deacons {Diakonous} likewise must be dignified, not double-tongued or given to much wine or greedy for money.
1 Timothy 3:9	They must hold to the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience.
1 Timothy 3:10	Additionally, they must first be tested. Then, if they are above reproach, let them serve as deacons.
1 Timothy 3:11	In the same way, the women (their wives) must be dignified, not slanderers, but temperate and faithful in all things.
1 Timothy 3:12	A deacon {Diakonoi} must be the husband of but one wife, a good manager of his children and of his own household.
1 Timothy 3:13	For those who have served well as deacons acquire for themselves a high standing and great confidence in the faith that is in Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves).
1 Timothy 3:14	Although I hope to come to you soon, I am writing you these things
1 Timothy 3:15	in case I am delayed, so that you will know how each one must conduct himself in God’s {Theou} household, which is the church {ekklēsia} of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.
1 Timothy 3:16	By common confession, the mystery of godliness is great: He appeared [God appeared] in the flesh, was vindicated (rendered innocent) by the Spirit (vindicated in spirit), was seen by angels (messengers), was proclaimed among the nations {ethnesin}, was believed in throughout the world, was taken up in glory {doxē}.
1 Timothy 4:1	Now the Spirit {pneuma} expressly states that in later times some will abandon the faith to follow deceitful spirits {pneumasin} and the teachings {didaskaliais} of demons,
1 Timothy 4:2	influenced by the hypocrisy of liars, whose consciences are seared with a hot iron.
1 Timothy 4:3	They will prohibit marriage and require abstinence from certain foods that God {Theos} has created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.
1 Timothy 4:4	For every creation of God {Theou} is good, and nothing that is received with thanksgiving should be rejected,
1 Timothy 4:5	because it is sanctified by the word of God {Theou} and prayer.
1 Timothy 4:6	By pointing out these things to the brothers (and sisters), you will be a good servant {diakonos} of Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves), nourished by the words of faith and sound instruction {didaskalias} that you have followed.
1 Timothy 4:7	But reject irreverent, silly myths. Instead, train yourself for godliness.
1 Timothy 4:8	For physical exercise is of limited value, but godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for the present life and for the one to come.
1 Timothy 4:9	This is a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance.
1 Timothy 4:10	To this end we labor and strive [and suffer reproach], because we have set our hope on the living God {Theō}, who is the Savior {Sōtēr} of everyone, and especially of those who believe.
1 Timothy 4:11	Command and teach {didaske} these things.
1 Timothy 4:12	Let no one despise your youth, but set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love {agapē}, in faith, in purity.
1 Timothy 4:13	Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, and to teaching {didaskalia}.
1 Timothy 4:14	Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given you through the prophecy spoken over you at the laying on of the hands of the elders.
1 Timothy 4:15	Be diligent in these matters and absorbed in them, so that your progress will be evident to all.
1 Timothy 4:16	Pay close attention to your life and to your teaching {didaskalia}. Persevere in these things, for by so doing you will save both yourself and those who hear you.
1 Timothy 5:1	Do not rebuke an older man, but appeal to him as to a father {patera}. Treat younger men as brothers,
1 Timothy 5:2	older women as mothers, and younger women as sisters, with absolute purity.
1 Timothy 5:3	Honor the widows who are truly widows.
1 Timothy 5:4	But if a widow has children or grandchildren, they must first learn to show godliness to their own family and repay their parents, for this is pleasing in the sight of God {Theou}.
1 Timothy 5:5	The widow who is truly in need and left all alone puts her hope in God {Theon} and continues night and day in her petitions and prayers.
1 Timothy 5:6	But she who lives for pleasure is dead even while she is still alive.
1 Timothy 5:7	Give these instructions to the believers, so that they will be above reproach.
1 Timothy 5:8	If anyone does not provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
1 Timothy 5:9	A widow should be enrolled if she is at least sixty years old, faithful to her husband,
1 Timothy 5:10	and well known for good deeds (acts) such as bringing up children, entertaining strangers, washing the feet of the saints (holy ones), imparting relief to the afflicted, and devoting herself to every good work.
1 Timothy 5:11	But refuse to enroll younger widows. For when their passions draw them away from Christ (the Anointed One), they will want to marry,
1 Timothy 5:12	and thus will incur judgment because they are setting aside their first faith.
1 Timothy 5:13	At the same time they will also learn to be idle, going from house to house and being not only idle, but also gossips and busybodies, discussing things they should not mention.
1 Timothy 5:14	So I advise the younger widows to marry, have children, and manage their households, denying the adversary occasion for slander.
1 Timothy 5:15	For some have already turned aside to follow Satan (the adversary).
1 Timothy 5:16	If any believing woman has dependent widows, she must assist them and not allow the church {ekklēsia} to be burdened, so that it can help the widows who are truly in need.
1 Timothy 5:17	Elders who lead effectively are worthy of double honor, especially those who work hard at preaching and teaching {didaskalia}.
1 Timothy 5:18	For the Scripture says, “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain <Deu 25:4>,” and, “The worker is worthy of his wages <Luk 10:7>.”
1 Timothy 5:19	Do not entertain an accusation against an elder, except on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
1 Timothy 5:20	But those who persist in sin should be rebuked in front of everyone, so that the others will stand in fear of sin.
1 Timothy 5:21	I solemnly charge you before God {Theou} and Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves) and the elect angels (messengers) to maintain these principles without bias, and to do nothing out of partiality.
1 Timothy 5:22	Do not be too quick in the laying on of hands and thereby share in the sins of others. Keep yourself pure.
1 Timothy 5:23	Stop drinking only water and use a little wine instead, because of your stomach and your frequent ailments.
1 Timothy 5:24	The sins of some men are obvious, going ahead of them to judgment; but the sins of others do not surface until later.
1 Timothy 5:25	In the same way, good deeds (acts) are obvious, and even the ones that are inconspicuous cannot remain hidden.
1 Timothy 6:1	All who are under the yoke of slavery should regard their masters {despotas} as fully worthy of honor, so that God’s {Theou} name and our teaching {didaskalia} will not be discredited (blasphemed).
1 Timothy 6:2	Those who have believing masters {despotas} should not show disrespect because they are brothers, but should serve them all the more, since those receiving their good service are beloved {agapētoi} believers. Teach {didaske} and encourage these principles.
1 Timothy 6:3	If anyone teaches another doctrine and disagrees with the sound words of our Lord {Kyriou} Jesus (YHWH saves) Christ (the Anointed One) and with godly teaching {didaskalia},
1 Timothy 6:4	he is conceited and understands nothing. Instead, he has an unhealthy interest in controversies and disputes about words, out of which come envy, strife, abusive talk, evil suspicions,
1 Timothy 6:5	and constant friction between men of depraved mind who are devoid of the truth. These men regard godliness as a means of gain [Withdraw yourself from such.].
1 Timothy 6:6	Of course, godliness with contentment is great gain.
1 Timothy 6:7	For we brought nothing into the world, so [so certainly] we cannot carry anything out of it.
1 Timothy 6:8	But if we have food and clothing, we will be content with these.
1 Timothy 6:9	Those who want to be rich, however, fall into temptation and become ensnared by many foolish and harmful desires that plunge them into ruin and destruction (ruin).
1 Timothy 6:10	For the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil. By craving it, some have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many sorrows.
1 Timothy 6:11	But you, O man of God {Theou}, flee from these things and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love {agapēn}, perseverance (endurance), and gentleness.
1 Timothy 6:12	Fight the good fight of the faith. Take hold of the eternal life to which you were called when you made the good confession before many witnesses.
1 Timothy 6:13	I charge you in the presence of God {Theou}, who gives life to all things, and of Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves), who made the good confession in His testimony before Pontius Pilate (armed with a spear):
1 Timothy 6:14	Keep this commandment without stain or reproach until the appearance of our Lord {Kyriou} Jesus (YHWH saves) Christ (the Anointed One),
1 Timothy 6:15	which the blessed and only Sovereign One—the King of kings and Lord {Kyrios} of lords—will bring about in His own time.
1 Timothy 6:16	He alone is immortal and dwells in unapproachable light. No one has ever seen Him, nor can anyone see Him. To Him be honor and eternal dominion! Amen.
1 Timothy 6:17	Instruct those who are rich in the present age not to be conceited and not to put their hope in the uncertainty of wealth, but in God {Theō}, who richly provides all things for us to enjoy.
1 Timothy 6:18	Instruct them to do good, to be rich in good works (acts), and to be generous and ready to share,
1 Timothy 6:19	treasuring up for themselves a firm foundation for the future, so that they may take hold of that which is truly life.
1 Timothy 6:20	O Timothy (honoring God), guard what has been entrusted to you. Avoid irreverent, empty chatter and the opposing arguments of so-called “knowledge,
1 Timothy 6:21	which some have professed and thus swerved away from the faith. Grace be with you⁺ all [Amen.].
2 Timothy 1:1	Paul (humble), an apostle (sent one) of Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves) by the will of God {Theou}, according to the promise of life in Christ Jesus,
2 Timothy 1:2	To Timothy (honoring God), my beloved {agapētō} child: Grace, mercy (compassion), and peace from God {Theou} the Father and Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves) our Lord {Kyriou}.
2 Timothy 1:3	I thank God {Theō}, whom I serve with a clear conscience as did my forefathers, as I constantly remember you night and day in my prayers.
2 Timothy 1:4	Recalling your tears, I long to see you so that I may be filled with joy.
2 Timothy 1:5	I am reminded of your sincere faith, which first dwelt in your grandmother Lois (more desirable) and your mother Eunice (good victory), and I am convinced is in you as well.
2 Timothy 1:6	For this reason I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God {Theou}, which is in you through the laying on of my hands.
2 Timothy 1:7	For God {Theos} has not given us a spirit {pneuma} of fear (timidity), but of power {dynameōs}, love {agapēs}, and self-control.
2 Timothy 1:8	So do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord {Kyriou}, or of me, His prisoner. Instead, join me in suffering for the gospel (good news) by the power {dynamin} of God {Theou}.
2 Timothy 1:9	He has saved us and called us to a holy (set apart) calling, not because of our works (acts), but by His own purpose and by the grace He granted us in Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves) before time began \before times eternal/.
2 Timothy 1:10	And now He has revealed this grace through the appearing of our Savior, Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves), who has abolished death and illuminated the way to life and immortality through the gospel (good news),
2 Timothy 1:11	to which I was appointed as a preacher, an apostle (sent one), and a teacher {didaskalos}.
2 Timothy 1:12	For this reason, even though I suffer as I do, I am not ashamed; for I know whom I have believed, and I am convinced that He is able to guard what I have entrusted to Him (what He has entrusted to me) for that day.
2 Timothy 1:13	Hold on to the pattern of sound teaching \sound words/ you have heard from me, with the faith and love {agapē} that are in Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves).
2 Timothy 1:14	Guard the treasure entrusted to you (the good deposit entrusted to you), with the help of the Holy Spirit {Hagiou Pneumatos} who dwells in us.
2 Timothy 1:15	You know that everyone in the Province of Asia \in Asia/ has deserted me, including Phygelus and Hermogenes.
2 Timothy 1:16	May the Lord {Kyrios} grant mercy (compassion) to the household of Onesiphorus (bringing advantage), because he has often refreshed me and was unashamed of my chains.
2 Timothy 1:17	Indeed, when he arrived in Rome, he searched diligently until he found me.
2 Timothy 1:18	May the Lord {Kyrios} grant Onesiphorus His mercy (compassion) on that day. You know very well how much he ministered to me in Ephesus (appealing).
2 Timothy 2:1	You therefore, my child, be strong in the grace that is in Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves).
2 Timothy 2:2	And the things that you have heard me say among many witnesses, entrust these to faithful men who will be qualified to teach {didaxai} others as well.
2 Timothy 2:3	Join me in suffering, like a good soldier of Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves).
2 Timothy 2:4	A soldier refrains from entangling himself in civilian affairs, in order to please the one who enlisted him.
2 Timothy 2:5	Likewise, a competitor does not receive the crown unless he competes according to the rules.
2 Timothy 2:6	The hardworking farmer should be the first to partake of the crops.
2 Timothy 2:7	Consider what I am saying, for the Lord {Kyrios} will give you insight into all things.
2 Timothy 2:8	Remember Jesus (YHWH saves) Christ (the Anointed One), raised from the dead, descended from David (beloved), as proclaimed by my gospel (good news),
2 Timothy 2:9	for which I suffer to the extent of being chained like a criminal. But the word of God {Theou} cannot be chained!
2 Timothy 2:10	For this reason I endure all things for the sake of the elect, so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves), with eternal glory {doxēs}.
2 Timothy 2:11	This is a trustworthy saying: If we died with Him, we will also live with Him;
2 Timothy 2:12	if we endure, we will also reign with Him; if we deny Him, He will also deny us;
2 Timothy 2:13	if we are faithless, He remains faithful, for He cannot deny Himself.
2 Timothy 2:14	Remind the believers of these things, charging them before God [the Lord] to avoid quarreling over words, which succeeds only in leading the listeners to ruin.
2 Timothy 2:15	Make every effort to present yourself approved to God {Theō}, an unashamed workman who accurately handles the word of truth.
2 Timothy 2:16	But avoid irreverent, empty chatter, which will only lead to more ungodliness,
2 Timothy 2:17	and the talk of such men will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus (beloved),
2 Timothy 2:18	who have deviated from the truth. They say that the resurrection (rising again) has already occurred, and they undermine the faith of some.
2 Timothy 2:19	Nevertheless, God’s {Theou} firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: “The Lord {Kyrios} knows those who are His <Num 16:5>,” and, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord {Kyriou} must turn away from iniquity.”
2 Timothy 2:20	A large house contains not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay. Some indeed are for honorable use, but others are for common use.
2 Timothy 2:21	So if anyone cleanses himself of what is unfit \cleanses himself of these/, he will be a vessel for honor: sanctified, useful to the Master {despotē}, and prepared for every good work.
2 Timothy 2:22	Flee from youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love {agapēn}, and peace, together with those who call on the Lord {Kyrion} out of a pure heart.
2 Timothy 2:23	But reject foolish and ignorant speculation, for you know that it breeds quarreling.
2 Timothy 2:24	And a servant {doulon} of the Lord {Kyriou} must not be quarrelsome, but must be kind to everyone, able to teach {didaktikon}, and forbearing.
2 Timothy 2:25	He must gently reprove those who oppose him, in the hope that God {Theos} may grant them repentance leading to a knowledge (discernment) of the truth.
2 Timothy 2:26	Then they will come to their senses and escape the snare of the devil {diabolou}, who has taken them captive to his will.
2 Timothy 3:1	But understand this: In the last days terrible times will come.
2 Timothy 3:2	For men will be lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, abusive (blasphemous), disobedient to their parents, ungrateful, unholy,
2 Timothy 3:3	unloving, unforgiving, slanderous, without self-control, brutal, without love of good,
2 Timothy 3:4	traitorous, reckless, conceited, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God,
2 Timothy 3:5	having a form of godliness but denying its power {dynamin}. Turn away from such as these!
2 Timothy 3:6	They are the kind who worm their way into households and captivate vulnerable women who are weighed down with sins and led astray by various passions,
2 Timothy 3:7	who are always learning but never able to come to a knowledge (discernment) of the truth.
2 Timothy 3:8	Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses <Jasher 79:27>, so also these men oppose the truth. They are depraved in mind and disqualified from the faith.
2 Timothy 3:9	But they will not advance much further. For just like Jannes and Jambres, their folly will be plain to everyone.
2 Timothy 3:10	You, however, have observed my teaching {didaskalia}, my conduct, my purpose, my faith, my patience, my love {agapē}, my perseverance (endurance),
2 Timothy 3:11	my persecutions, and the sufferings that came upon me in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. What persecutions I endured! Yet the Lord {Kyrios} rescued me from all of them.
2 Timothy 3:12	Indeed, all who desire to live godly lives in Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves) will be persecuted,
2 Timothy 3:13	while evil men and imposters go from bad to worse, deceiving and being deceived.
2 Timothy 3:14	But as for you, continue in the things you have learned and firmly believed, since you know from whom you have learned them.
2 Timothy 3:15	From infancy you have known the Holy Scriptures, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves).
2 Timothy 3:16	All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for instruction {didaskalian}, for conviction, for correction, and for training in righteousness,
2 Timothy 3:17	so that the man of God {Theou} may be complete, fully equipped for every good work.
2 Timothy 4:1	I charge you in the presence of God {Theou} and of Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves), who will judge the living and the dead, and in view of His appearing and His kingdom:
2 Timothy 4:2	Preach the word; be prepared in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, and encourage with every form of patient instruction {didachē}.
2 Timothy 4:3	For the time will come when men will not tolerate sound doctrine {didaskalias}, but with itching ears they will gather around themselves teachers {didaskalous} to suit their own desires.
2 Timothy 4:4	So they will turn their ears away from the truth and turn aside to myths.
2 Timothy 4:5	But you, be sober in all things, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill your ministry {diakonian}.
2 Timothy 4:6	For I am already being poured out like a drink offering, and the time of my departure is at hand.
2 Timothy 4:7	I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
2 Timothy 4:8	From now on there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord {kyrios}, the righteous Judge, will award to me on that day—and not only to me, but to all who crave {ēgapēkosi} His appearing.
2 Timothy 4:9	Make every effort to come to me quickly,
2 Timothy 4:10	because Demas, in his love of this world, has deserted me and gone to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia (Land of the Gauls), and Titus (title of honor) to Dalmatia.
2 Timothy 4:11	Only Luke (from Lucania) is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, because he is useful to me in the ministry {diakonian}.
2 Timothy 4:12	Tychicus, however, I have sent to Ephesus (appealing).
2 Timothy 4:13	When you come, bring the cloak that I left with Carpus (fruit) at Troas, and my scrolls (papyrus rolls), especially the parchments.
2 Timothy 4:14	Alexander (defending men) the coppersmith did great harm to me. The Lord {Kyrios} will repay him according to his deeds (acts).
2 Timothy 4:15	You too should beware of him, for he has vigorously opposed our message.
2 Timothy 4:16	At my first defense, no one stood with me, but everyone deserted me. May it not be charged against them.
2 Timothy 4:17	But the Lord {Kyrios} stood by me and strengthened me, so that through me the message would be fully proclaimed, and all the Gentiles {ethnē} would hear it. So I was delivered from the mouth of the lion.
2 Timothy 4:18	And the Lord {Kyrios} will rescue me from every evil action and bring me safely into His heavenly kingdom. To Him be the glory {doxa} forever \to the ages/ and ever. Amen.
2 Timothy 4:19	Greet Prisca (Priscilla) and Aquila (eagle), as well as the household of Onesiphorus (bringing advantage).
2 Timothy 4:20	Erastus (lovely) has remained at Corinth (in Greece), and Trophimus (nourishing) I left sick in Miletus.
2 Timothy 4:21	Make every effort to come to me before winter. Eubulus sends you greetings, as do Pudens (bashful), Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers.
2 Timothy 4:22	The Lord {Kyrios} be with your spirit {pneumatos}. Grace be with you⁺ all [Amen.].
Titus 1:1	Paul (humble), a servant {doulos} of God {Theou} and an apostle (sent one) of Jesus (YHWH saves) Christ (the Anointed One) for the faith of God’s elect and their knowledge (discernment) of the truth that leads to godliness,
Titus 1:2	in the hope of eternal life, which God {Theos}, who cannot lie, promised before time began \before times eternal/.
Titus 1:3	In His own time He has made His word evident in the proclamation entrusted to me by the command of God {Theou} our Savior.
Titus 1:4	To Titus (title of honor), my true child in our common faith: Grace and peace from God {Theou} the Father and Christ (the Anointed One) Jesus (YHWH saves) our Savior.
Titus 1:5	The reason I left you in Crete was that you would set in order what was unfinished and appoint elders in every town, as I directed you.
Titus 1:6	An elder must be blameless, the husband of but one wife (faithful to his wife), having children who are believers and who are not open to accusation of indiscretion or insubordination.
Titus 1:7	As God’s {Theou} steward, an overseer must be above reproach—not self-willed, not quick-tempered, not given to drunkenness, not violent, not greedy for money.
Titus 1:8	Instead, he must be hospitable, a lover of good {philagathon}, self-controlled, upright, holy, and disciplined.
Titus 1:9	He must hold firmly to the faithful word as it was taught {didachēn}, so that he can encourage others by sound teaching {didaskalia} and refute those who contradict it.
Titus 1:10	For many are rebellious and full of empty talk and deception, especially those of the circumcision,
Titus 1:11	who must be silenced. For the sake of dishonorable gain, they undermine entire households and teach {didaskontes} things they should not.
Titus 1:12	As one of their own prophets has said, “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons (the Epimenides paradox).”
Titus 1:13	This testimony is true. Therefore rebuke them sternly, so that they will be sound in the faith
Titus 1:14	and will pay no attention to Jewish myths or to the commands of men who have rejected the truth.
Titus 1:15	To the pure, all things are pure; but to the defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure. Indeed, both their minds and their consciences are defiled.
Titus 1:16	They profess to know God {Theon}, but by their actions (acts) they deny Him. They are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good deed.
Titus 2:1	But as for you, speak the things that are consistent with sound doctrine {didaskalia}.
Titus 2:2	Older men are to be temperate, dignified, self-controlled, and sound in faith, love {agapē}, and perseverance (endurance).
Titus 2:3	Older women, likewise, are to be reverent in their behavior, not slanderers or addicted to much wine, but teachers of good.
Titus 2:4	In this way they can train the young women to love their husbands and children,

Philemon 1:12	I am sending back to you him who is my very heart.
Philemon 1:13	I would have liked to keep him with me, so that on your behalf he could minister to me in my chains for the gospel (good news).
Philemon 1:14	But I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your goodness will not be out of compulsion, but by your own free will.

Philemon 1:18	But if he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge it to my account.
Philemon 1:19	I, Paul (humble), write this with my own hand. I will repay it—not to mention that you owe me your very self.
Philemon 1:20	Yes, brother, let me have some benefit {onaim&#275;n} from you in the Lord {Kyriō}. Refresh my heart in Christ (the Anointed One).
Philemon 1:21	Confident of your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I ask.

Hebrews 1:3	The Son is the radiance of God’s glory {doxēs} and the exact representation of His nature, upholding all things by His powerful word {rhēmati}. After He had provided purification for sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.
Hebrews 1:4	So He became as far superior to the angels (messengers) as the name He has inherited is excellent beyond theirs.
Hebrews 1:5	For to which of the angels (messengers) did God ever say: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father <Psa 2:7>” Or again: “I will be His Father {Patera}, and He will be My Son <2Sa 7:14; 1Ch 17:13>”
Hebrews 1:6	And again, when God brings His firstborn into the world, He says: “Let all God’s {Theou} angels (messengers) worship Him <Deu 32:43>.”

Hebrews 1:8	But about the Son He says: “Your throne, O God {Theos}, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom.

Hebrews 1:10	And: “In the beginning, O Lord {Kyrie}, You laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.
Hebrews 1:11	They will perish, but You remain; they will all wear out like a garment.

Hebrews 1:14	Are not the angels \Are they not all/ ministering spirits {pneumata} sent to serve {diakonian} those who will inherit salvation?

Hebrews 2:2	For if the message spoken by angels (messengers) was binding, and every transgression and disobedience received its just punishment,
Hebrews 2:3	how shall we escape if we neglect such a great salvation? This salvation was first announced by the Lord {Kyriou}, was confirmed to us by those who heard Him,
Hebrews 2:4	and was affirmed by God {Theou} through signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit {Hagiou Pneumatos} distributed according to His will.
Hebrews 2:5	For it is not to angels (messengers) that He has subjected the world to come, about which we are speaking.

Hebrews 2:9	But we see Jesus (YHWH saves), who was made a little lower than the angels (messengers), now crowned with glory {doxē} and honor because He suffered death, so that by the grace of God {Theou} He might taste death for everyone.

Hebrews 2:15	and free those who all their lives were held in slavery by their fear of death.
Hebrews 2:16	For surely it is not the angels (messengers) He helps, but the descendants (seed) of Abraham (father of many).
Hebrews 2:17	For this reason He had to be made like His brothers in every way, so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in service to God {Theon}, in order to make atonement (to make propitiation) for the sins of the people.

Hebrews 7:1	This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God {Theou} Most High <Gen 14:18>. He met Abraham (father of many) returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,
Hebrews 7:2	and Abraham (father of many) apportioned to him a tenth of everything. First, his name means “king of righteousness. Then also, “king of Salem means “king of peace.
Hebrews 7:3	Without father or mother or genealogy, without beginning of days or end of life, like the Son of God {Theou}, he remains a priest for all time.
Hebrews 7:4	Consider how great Melchizedek was: Even the patriarch Abraham (father of many) gave him a tenth of the plunder.
Hebrews 7:5	Now the law commands the sons of Levi (attached to) who become priests to collect a tenth from the people—that is, from their brothers—though they too are descended from Abraham (father of many).
Hebrews 7:6	But Melchizedek, who did not trace his descent from Levi, collected a tenth from Abraham (father of many) and blessed him who had the promises.
Hebrews 7:7	And indisputably, the lesser is blessed by the greater.
Hebrews 7:8	In the case of the Levites, mortal men collect the tenth; but in the case of Melchizedek, it is affirmed that he lives on.
Hebrews 7:9	And so to speak, Levi (attached to), who collects the tenth, paid the tenth through Abraham (father of many).
Hebrews 7:10	For when Melchizedek met Abraham (father of many), Levi was still in the loin of his ancestor.
Hebrews 7:11	Now if perfection could have been attained through the Levitical priesthood (for on this basis the people received the law), why was there still need for another priest to appear—one in the order of Melchizedek and not in the order of Aaron (exalted)?
Hebrews 7:12	For when the priesthood is changed, the law must be changed as well.
Hebrews 7:13	He of whom these things are said belonged to a different tribe, from which no one has ever served at the altar.
Hebrews 7:14	For it is clear that our Lord {Kyrios} descended from Judah (praise), a tribe as to which Moses (drawn out) said nothing about priests.
Hebrews 7:15	And this point is even more clear if another priest like Melchizedek appears,
Hebrews 7:16	one who has become a priest not by a law of succession, but by the power {dynamin} of an indestructible life.
Hebrews 7:17	For it is testified: “You are a priest forever \to the age/ in the order of Melchizedek <Psa 110:4>.”
Hebrews 7:18	So the former commandment is set aside because it was weak and useless
Hebrews 7:19	(for the law made nothing perfect), and a better hope is introduced, by which we draw near to God {Theō}.
Hebrews 7:20	And none of this happened without an oath. For others became priests without an oath,
Hebrews 7:21	but Jesus became a priest with an oath by the One who said to Him: “The Lord {Kyrios} has sworn and will not change His mind: ‘You are a priest forever <Psa 110:4>.’”
Hebrews 7:22	Because of this oath, Jesus (YHWH saves) has become the guarantee of a better covenant {diathēkēs}.
Hebrews 7:23	Now there have been many other priests, since death prevented them from continuing in office.
Hebrews 7:24	But because Jesus lives forever \to the age/, He has a permanent priesthood.
Hebrews 7:25	Therefore He is able to save completely (forever) those who draw near to God {Theō} through Him, since He always lives to intercede for them.
Hebrews 7:26	Such a high priest truly befits us—One who is holy, innocent, undefiled, set apart from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.
Hebrews 7:27	Unlike the other high priests, He does not need to offer daily sacrifices, first for His own sins and then for the sins of the people; He sacrificed for sin once for all when He offered up Himself.
Hebrews 7:28	For the law appoints as high priests men who are weak; but the oath, which came after the law, appointed the Son, who has been made perfect forever \to the age/.
